What number is missing from the boxes in the statement below?

The ratio of squares to circles is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14133433/assets/296da85a5c6d0f5cf14f8fe144b0cdf66e4082b425b886d98fcbe672a2e8a190.svg) because there is $1$ square for every ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14133433/assets/b1fda7079b1445faec7a1a2bb2abcafd9147f8a28863a2618c66166cea102a14.svg) circle(s).
question.worked_solution:
First, we count the number of squares. We see that there are $2$ squares.

Then, we count the number of circles. We see that there are $2$ circles.

So the ratio of circles to squares is $2:2.$

We can simplify this ratio by dividing both numbers by $2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,2 &  & : & \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,2 &  \\ \,\,↓÷\,\,2 &  &  &  & \,\,\,↓÷\,\,2 &  \\ \,\,1 &  & : &  & \,\,\,1 & \end{aligned}
$$

This means that $2:2$ is equivalent to $1:1.$ 

So, the complete statement is
"The ratio of squares to circles is $1:\bbox[3px,#d3d3d3]{1}\,$ because there is $1$ square for every $\bbox[3px,#d3d3d3]{1}\,$circle."
